CVE-2026-123806.title: python-tuf: Platform-dependent delegation path matching
CVE-2026-123806.description: python-tuf is a Python reference implementation of The Update Framework (TUF). CVE-2026-134846.title: pgjdbc GSS encryption accepts replayed packets and can stop encrypting
CVE-2026-134846.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an earlier server packet from the same connection, and the driver accepts it as the answer to the current query. Only connections with gssEncMode=prefer or require that start GSS encryption are affected. Versions 42.2.15 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

CVE-2026-62156.title: hdfs_fdw HiveQL injection through pushed-down IN and = ANY(array) string literals
CVE-2026-62156.description: hdfs_fdw builds string literals for IN and = ANY(array) clauses pushed down to the remote Hive or Spark server without escaping single quotes. An authenticated user with only SELECT on a foreign table can supply a crafted array value that breaks out of the literal and changes the HiveQL query, which then runs on the remote server with the foreign server's credentials. The same release fixes two lower-severity issues: the JDBC connection string, including the trustStorePassword value, was written to logs, and credentials stayed in memory in cleartext after the connection was established. The issue is fixed in hdfs_fdw 2.4.0. From hdfs_fdw 2.4.0, hdfs_fdw escapes single quotes in these literals, masks trustStorePassword in logs and clears credentials from memory after connecting.

CVE-2026-99420.title: ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs
CVE-2026-99420.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs

An unprivileged user crashes the kernel by mounting overlayfs with the
volatile option.

A dentry that serves as the parent of a lookup must be a directory.
ovl_create_volatile_dirty() walks work/incompat/volatile/dirty by name,
and ovl_lookup_or_create() returns an existing entry whatever its type.
A file or a symlink that another task creates during the mount becomes
the parent of the next lookup, which calls a NULL ->lookup.

An unprivileged user mounted overlayfs with "volatile" in a user
namespace while a second process created a symlink named work/incompat,
and the mount task oopsed on a NULL ->lookup call.

Fix this by returning -ENOTDIR from ovl_lookup_or_create() when the
caller asked for a directory and the existing entry is a non-dir.

f2fs: release a removed xattr node in roll-forward recovery

the file is then fsynced without a checkpoint, only the inode block is
written, with i_xattr_nid of 0.

Roll-forward recovery starts from the checkpointed inode, whose
i_xattr_nid still points to the old xattr node.

the stale xattr node:

xattr space after end of list".

its terminator is read from the stale node, and the removed xattrs
come back after recovery.

can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock()

The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options are copied from and
to user space while holding lock_sock(). A copy that faults or stalls,

CVE-2026-99745.title: x86/bugs: Select the BHI mitigation based on the attack vector properly
CVE-2026-99745.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

x86/bugs: Select the BHI mitigation based on the attack vector properly

The BHI mitigation selection is inconsistent with the documentation
(attack_vector_controls.rst), which lists BHI under both the
user->kernel and guest->host attack vectors. bhi_select_mitigation()
only enables it when CPU_MITIGATE_GUEST_HOST is set; otherwise it
selects BHI_MITIGATION_OFF, even if CPU_MITIGATE_USER_KERNEL is set.

As a result, a kernel compiled with KVM disabled gets BHI automatically
disabled, since CPU_MITIGATE_GUEST_HOST defaults to off without KVM.
This is a bug, given that CPU_MITIGATE_USER_KERNEL still needs it: on
affected Intel CPUs these kernels lose BHI_DIS_S or the BHB clearing
loop by default. Booting with mitigations=auto,no_guest_host has the
same effect.

Select BHI_MITIGATION_ON whenever user->kernel is mitigated, and keep
BHI_MITIGATION_VMEXIT_ONLY for the guest->host-only case.

CVE-2026-99806.title: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject mode changes on connected channels
CVE-2026-99806.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject mode changes on connected channels

A peer can send a configuration response with an RFC
option for another mode to a connected channel, for
example to switch it from Streaming to ERTM mode.
l2cap_parse_conf_rsp() then changes chan->mode, but
l2cap_ertm_init() is not called again, so the ERTM
sequence lists are never allocated. The next
out-of-sequence I-frame makes l2cap_seq_list_clear()
write through the NULL srej_list.list.

Refuse the channel when a response tries to change
the mode of a connected channel.
